claim_ceiling: This manifest defines a research campaign and abstract scenario archetypes only. It contains no site measurements, approved engineering design, local price data, real utility routes, or field performance claims.

architecture_candidates.name: Observed local practice
architecture_candidates.description: Capture the actual route-specific utility, protection, maintenance and restoration workflow as the baseline; do not replace observations with an idealized textbook baseline.

architecture_candidates.name: Protected overhead or exposed route
architecture_candidates.description: Evaluate targeted physical hardening, access control, tamper detection and response while retaining an overhead or exposed asset route.

architecture_candidates.name: Conventional single-utility underground
architecture_candidates.description: Evaluate a buried single-utility installation using conventional access, inspection and repair practices.

architecture_candidates.name: Shared partitioned duct bank
architecture_candidates.description: Evaluate co-ordinated installation of physically segregated utility ducts with conventional maintenance access.

architecture_candidates.name: Robot-first duct bank and service nodes
architecture_candidates.description: Evaluate standardized robot-accessible routes, modular components, docking, inspection and pull-through replacement subject to exact physical qualification.

architecture_candidates.name: Accessible mini-gallery or multi-utility tunnel
architecture_candidates.description: Evaluate an accessible service gallery only where utility density, criticality and repeat intervention frequency may justify its added capital and operating requirements.

architecture_candidates.name: Existing corridor or brownfield reuse
architecture_candidates.description: Evaluate reuse or refurbishment of existing conduits, tunnels or brownfield assets after geotechnical, hydrogeological, environmental, legal and serviceability gates.

architecture_candidates.name: No-build, repair-only or targeted hardening
architecture_candidates.description: Retain no-build and limited intervention as valid outcomes when new underground infrastructure is ineligible or not economically justified.

site_archetypes.name: Multi-tenant industrial precinct
characteristics: measurable service availability and economic throughput

site_archetypes.name: Developing settlement and expansion edge
characteristics: need for incremental deployment and local maintenance capability

benchmark_suites.name: Spatial evidence and conflict discovery
benchmark_suites.purpose: Measure whether route geometry, utility identity, coordinate reference, source quality and unknown extents are preserved and correctly used.
metrics: horizontal and vertical geometry error against surveyed or exposed truth
route coverage and unknown extent
critical crossing detection and false-clear rate
CRS datum unit and epoch mismatch rejection
uncertainty interval coverage
cost and time per accepted metre mapped
adversarial_cases: legacy drawing presented as verified as-built
wrong coordinate reference or vertical datum
missing utility record silently treated as empty corridor

benchmark_suites.name: Construction and installation
benchmark_suites.purpose: Compare eligible construction methods on accepted work and whole-workflow cost, not nominal machine production.
metrics: accepted installed metres per shift
total cost per accepted metre
utility strikes and settlement
mobilization traffic spoil and reinstatement cost
service interruption and rework
as-built discrepancy and completeness

benchmark_suites.name: Robotic inspection and maintenance
benchmark_suites.purpose: Qualify robot coverage, localization, observation quality, inspection outputs, safe recovery and independently accepted maintenance.
metrics: observed unobserved unusable and not-reached route length
position and chainage P50 P95 and maximum error
per-class precision recall and critical-defect false-negative rate
defect dimensional error and uncertainty calibration
mission completion and safe return
energy per metre and human review minutes
first-pass repair acceptance and rework
adversarial_cases: robot cannot turn or be retrieved

benchmark_suites.name: Theft and tamper resilience
benchmark_suites.purpose: Measure exposure-normalized theft, attempted tampering, detection, service impact, response and residual risk across physical architectures.
metrics: theft and attempted tamper per kilometre-year
direct loss and consequential service-hours lost
detection lead time and false alarms per kilometre-month
tamper localization error and response time
sectional isolation and restoration time
recurrence after intervention
lawful material recovery traceability
adversarial_cases: theft shifting to another material or asset class
flood or fire disables multiple protection layers
alarm occurs but no responder is available

benchmark_suites.name: Lifecycle economics and public value
benchmark_suites.purpose: Compare whole-life cost and delivered service under identical boundaries while accounting for uncertainty and local economic participation.
metrics: 10 20 and 30 year discounted NPV
equivalent annual cost
cost per accepted service-unit-year
break-even corridor occupancy and repeat-work frequency
P50 and P90 lifecycle cost
local labour hours wages supplier spend SME participation and training
adversarial_cases: correlated theft and outage losses omitted
local employment claimed without paid-hour evidence
provider exit with no maintenance capability

benchmark_suites.name: Assurance and interoperability
benchmark_suites.purpose: Verify exact inputs, source ownership, decision dispositions, independent oracle agreement and authority boundaries.
metrics: false acceptance of seeded hard constraints
unknown-to-clear promotion count
stale authority reuse count
claim-to-input-revision traceability
independent oracle agreement
silent coverage-gap count
adversarial_cases: simulation PASS promoted to construction approval
repair marked complete without independent observation
candidate generator also supplies its own reference answer

benchmark_suites.name: Wayleave and utility-owner coordination
benchmark_suites.purpose: Measure the evidence and elapsed-time performance of the real authority process without granting the software permission to approve work.
metrics: elapsed time for service inquiry service-owner response cross-cut planning wayleave decision and authorization
service-owner identification coverage before excavation
cross-cut confirmation / unresolved yield
design iteration count from previously unknown or conflicting services
utility strike near-miss damage and reinstatement defect rates
permit correction or rejection reasons
time from completion to accepted as-built
repeat road cuts avoided with verified work-order comparison
adversarial_cases: municipality-specific rule applied to another municipality
draft by-law mistaken for enacted rule
missing or expired wayleave treated as approval
cross-cut result not tied to surveyed location and coordinate frame
approved design revision differs from constructed revision
work performed outside permitted time or location

benchmark_suites.name: Utility cable-duct robot traversal and maintenance tooling
benchmark_suites.purpose: Qualify inspection, route localization, draw-rope placement, inert dummy-cable pull-through and safe recovery on exact non-energized duct profiles; do not transfer sewer-crawler metrics.
metrics: profile-specific route reachability and complete observation disposition
chainage P50 P95 and maximum error against rig truth
per-class obstruction detection and critical-blockage false-negative rate
dummy cable peak and integrated pulling force and bend-radius compliance
duct and dummy-cable pre/post damage findings
safe retrieval and recovery success within declared laboratory envelope
energy per accepted metre and human operator interventions
adversarial_cases: compound bend or coupling step outside tool envelope
tether snag or excess pull tension
robot immobilization in a non-retrievable location
stale calibration or wrong duct-profile revision
dummy cable has unknown mechanical limits

quantitative_inputs_required.evidence_required: site investigation and qualified interpretation for the selected method

quantitative_inputs_required.evidence_required: owner-issued asset records and inspections with quality state

quantitative_inputs_required.unit_or_representation: incident counts and exposure time normalized by asset length or asset-years
quantitative_inputs_required.evidence_required: utility security logs with incident definition, attempted/completed status, location precision and time window

quantitative_inputs_required.unit_or_representation: local currency, price year, duration and affected service units
quantitative_inputs_required.evidence_required: work orders, materials, labour, contractor costs and service-impact records

quantitative_inputs_required.unit_or_representation: local currency per accepted service unit with price year and route stratum
quantitative_inputs_required.evidence_required: current South African quotations or tender records broken down by method, geology, diameter, access and reinstatement

quantitative_inputs_required.unit_or_representation: versioned reach, geometry, load, speed, power, localization, environment and retrieval envelope
quantitative_inputs_required.evidence_required: vendor claim separated from calibrated bench result and independently qualified capability

quantitative_inputs_required.unit_or_representation: electrical ratings, geometry, joint types, thermal and mechanical limits, mass and lifecycle data
quantitative_inputs_required.evidence_required: manufacturer data plus applicable type tests, design calculation and utility acceptance

quantitative_inputs_required.unit_or_representation: capacity, occupancy, access rights, tariffs, service levels and cost allocation

comparison_rules: Compare the same required delivered service, quality, availability and route boundary.
Freeze cost year, currency, discount rate, financing assumptions, design life and replacement policy before ranking.
Report capital, operating, maintenance, theft, outage, restoration and decommissioning costs separately before calculating totals.
Run only physically and legally eligible candidates through economic ranking; unresolved hard constraints remain Indeterminate.
Use the same exogenous disturbance traces and resource budgets across paired candidate architectures.
Keep no-build, targeted hardening and conventional installation as valid outcomes.
Do not transfer sewer-robot results to cable ducts, water pipes or electrical networks without a matched evaluation.
Do not transfer historical UK multi-utility-tunnel or US trenchless unit costs directly to current South African projects.
Report uncertainty, denominator, rejected cases and unsupported cases; do not hide trade-offs in a single readiness score.
